title: The gospel as the rule (1208)
hookLine: Francis hears Matthew 10 at Mass and decides to live it literally

cards: A small chapel outside Assisi. A Mass. The priest reads the gospel, the same way gospels get read every day, and the room may well have heard this one before.
One man in the chapel hasn't heard it like this. It's the passage where Jesus sends his disciples out with almost nothing. When Mass ends, the man asks the priest to explain it.
And when the priest is done, he says, in his biographer's telling: this is what I want. This is what I've been looking for. Today: the gospel as the rule.

teach.h: NO GOLD, NO SCRIP, NO TWO COATS.
teach.b: Here's the passage, from Matthew, in the Douay-Rheims.

Jesus tells the twelve: "Do not possess gold, nor silver, nor money in your purses: Nor scrip for your journey, nor two coats, nor shoes, nor a staff; for the workman is worthy of his meat." A scrip is a traveler's bag.
So: no money, no bag, no spare coat, no shoes, no walking stick. Go, and trust that you'll be fed. Words like these can be heard as a picture of an attitude: hold things loosely.

teach.h: SHOES OFF, STAFF DOWN, A ROPE BELT.
teach.b: His early biographer says he took off his shoes on the spot, put down his staff, kept a single tunic, and swapped his leather belt for a piece of rope. Then he went from place to place, preaching peace and repentance.

teach.h: THE MOST HIGH REVEALED IT TO ME.
teach.b: Later, in his Testament, Francis said no one showed him what to do; the Most High himself revealed that he should live according to the form of the holy gospel. Benedict wrote a rule and pointed beyond it to Scripture.
Francis tried to skip the middle step.
When his brothers later needed a written rule, its opening line said, in effect: the rule and life of the brothers is this, to observe the holy gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.
The gospel wasn't the inspiration for the rule. It was the rule. The biographer doesn't say which gospel writer's version was read; the sending passages in Matthew, Mark and Luke are close cousins.

teach.h: HE HEARD IT AND DID IT.
teach.b: What he tells is the response: Francis heard it and did it, literally.

how: Franciscan friars take the gospel as their rule of life, and the Rule of Saint Francis opens by naming the observance of the holy gospel as the life of the brothers.

games.q: what does “the gospel as the rule” mean?
o: living the gospel's words as written, as your whole rule of life
a rule of life written to explain the gospel's harder sayings
reading the gospel aloud at every meal, as the monks did

games.q: the gospel as the rule — tap the pairs.

s: Francis read the sending passage as a loose picture of an attitude
he took it as instructions: shoes off, staff down, one tunic, a rope for a belt.
Francis's written rule says the brothers' life is to observe the gospel
its opening line names the holy gospel as the rule and life of the brothers.
the early biographer names Matthew as the gospel read that day
he speaks of the sending of the disciples without naming which gospel; Matthew, Mark and Luke all tell it.

games.q: you've just heard Jesus tell his disciples to take no money, no bag, no shoes, no staff. Mass is over. what do you do?
o: admire it, and go home the same.
ask the priest to explain it, then take off your shoes.
write a long commentary on what it might mean.
games.why: in his biographer's telling, Francis asked the priest to explain it, said this is what I want, and did it on the spot.

practice: Let one gospel line come to mind that you know so well it's gone smooth: give to the one who asks, love your enemies, take nothing for the journey.
Hold it the way Francis held his, not as a nice idea but as plain instruction, and let one concrete picture appear of what doing exactly this would look like. If you pray, ask for the nerve to do it.

wordCard.voice: The gospel as the rule. Francis's choice to live the gospel's words as written, starting with the sending of the twelve: take nothing for the journey. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: take nothing. Francis heard the sending of the twelve as words meant for him. Until tomorrow.
